title: Hidden among the baggage (1 Samuel 10:20–24)
hookLine: the tall new king hides from his own crowning

cards: The whole people is gathered at Mizpah, and Samuel names a king by lot, so everyone can watch it narrow down. The tribes come near, and the tribe of Benjamin is taken. Then the family of the Matrites.
Then one man: Saul, the son of Kish. Every eye turns to find him, and he isn't there. They look.
They call. Nothing. So they ask the LORD: has the man come here yet?
And the answer comes back: "Behold, he hath hid himself among the baggage."

teach.h: ANOINTED IN SECRET, TOLD NO ONE.
teach.b: Here's what makes it strange: Saul already knows. Samuel had taken him aside on the edge of town, poured oil on his head, and told him God had chosen him.
When Saul went home and his uncle asked what Samuel had said, Saul told him about the lost donkeys he'd been chasing, and nothing about the kingdom.
And before any of that, when Samuel first hinted at it, Saul said: am I not a Benjamite, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel, and isn't my family the least of them all?
Gideon said much the same, down in his winepress. So the lot can hardly surprise him. And he's hiding among the gear, the bags and supplies people brought.

teach.h: THE TALLEST MAN, BEHIND THE BAGS.
teach.b: The tallest man in Israel, crouched behind the luggage. The people run and fetch him, and when he stands among them, he's higher than any of them from his shoulders upward.
Samuel says: do you see the one the LORD has chosen? There's none like him. The people shout: long live the king.

teach.h: HOW SHALL THIS MAN SAVE US?
teach.b: Some worthless men say, how shall this man save us? They despise him and bring him no gift.

teach.h: HE HATH HID HIMSELF AMONG THE BAGGAGE.
teach.b: And Saul, the text says, held his peace. Readers hear his hiding in different ways: humility, a man who didn't want power, or fear, a man who knew how heavy it would be. The text doesn't decide.
It shows a man who looked like a king from the outside, crouched where no one could see him.

how: Jews read Saul's choosing at Mizpah as part of the Former Prophets; commentators differ on whether his hiding shows humility or fear.

o: the king found hiding among the baggage at Mizpah
the prophet who drew the lots for king at Mizpah
a Benjamite who refused the crown and went home

games.q: the lot at Mizpah — tap the pairs.
p: how shall this man save us?

s: Saul learned he would be king when the lot fell on him
Samuel had already anointed him in secret, and Saul told no one.
Saul was taller than everyone from his shoulders up
when he stood among the people, he was higher than any of them from his shoulders and upward.
Saul punished the men who despised him
the text says he held his peace.

games.q: you're Saul. you were anointed in secret, and now the lot is narrowing toward your name in front of the whole people. what do you do?
o: step forward before they call you.
games.why: he hides among the baggage, and they have to ask God where he is. then they run and fetch him, and he stands a head above them all.

practice: Think of something you've been asked to do, or know you're meant to do, that you keep ducking, leading something, speaking up, being the grown-up in a hard family moment, and notice where you've been hiding: busyness, jokes, the luggage.
Don't force a decision; just stand up from behind the bags in your mind, and let yourself be seen. If you pray, ask for the strength to stand.

wordCard.voice: Saul. The tall new king, already anointed in secret, found hiding among the baggage when the lot fell on him at Mizpah.
